title: Geo-aware accelerator affinity with soft spend boundaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a geo-aware routing controller that selects region + accelerator class with tenant-level soft spend boundaries. Goals: prefer low-cost preemptible/spot capacity when safe, respect latency SLOs, and gracefully degrade to on-demand SKUs or lower-capacity model variants when a tenant approaches a spend boundary. The feature must support per-tenant virtual wallets, accelerator affinity maps, and a chainable fallback policy for model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes region+accelerator recommendation API used by runtime routing
Per-tenant soft spend boundary enforced via throttling rather than hard reject
Fallback chain defined and exercised: preferred accelerator -> compatible accelerator -> lower-size model variant -> on-demand instance in alternate region
End-to-end integration test that simulates spot eviction and validates automatic variant fallback within 3s for 95th percentile requests
Dashboard shows per-tenant spend, headroom, and fallback counts with alerts when headroom < 10%
implementation_plan: Design: finalize affinity data model (region, accelerator class, SKU preference) and wallet semantics
Runtime: add AffinityPolicy evaluator in router (stateless recommendation + stateful wallet read/write)
Allocator: two-stage allocation: pass1 try spot-preferred placement, pass2 fall back to on-demand or variant routing
KV: add tenant->wallet in existing spender-store with leaky-bucket semantics
Testing: unit tests for evaluator, chaos test for spot eviction, integration test for wallet exhaustion behavior
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind config flag per-tenant
Start with opt-in alpha tenants in us-west-2 and europe-west1
Monitor fallback rates and tail latency for 72 hours
Expand to full cohort after 2 weeks with gradual percentage rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
risks: Wallet undercount race during heavy concurrent requests could allow overspend (mitigation: optimistic concurrency + periodic reconciliation)
Latency regression if allocation path adds synchronous wallet RPC (mitigation: local cache and async reconciliation)
Cold-starts when switching to on-demand in remote region (mitigation: warm pools and model variant prefetch)
metrics: 95th and 99th percentile token latency for served requests
